title_en: Calamos’ Nelson on Finding Fundamental Momentum
title_zh: Calamos 的纳尔逊谈发掘“基本面动能”
subtitle_zh: Calamos Investments 高级副总裁兼投资组合经理布兰登·纳尔逊（Brandon Nelson）拆解“基本面动能”选股法：可持续增长与被低估的增长如何共同催生中小盘大赢家。
description: Calamos’ Nelson on Finding Fundamental Momentum

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into the processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cohn. I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Some of the market's biggest companies started out much smaller, but investing in small and mid-cap growth companies isn't simply about trying to find the next company. They'll become a household name. These businesses can be earlier in their growth trajectories with less established track records and greater uncertainty about what their business may ultimately become. That can create opportunities for active managers, but that also puts a premium on determining which companies can sustain their growth and, just as importantly, what the market already expects from them. So today, I wanted to explore how an active manager approaches that challenge, how potential investments are identified in research, how sustainable growth is separated from short-term momentum, and how expectations and valuation factor into security selection and how those individual ideas come together in a portfolio. Joining me to discuss that is Brandon Nelson, Senior Vice President and Portfolio Manager at Calamos Investments, including the Calamos-Tapani Small Cap Growth Mutual Fund, ticker CTSIX, and the Calamos-Tapani Active SMID Growth Strategy, which just actually converted from a mutual fund to an ETF this week with the ticker CTAG, or C-T-A-G, and is actually the first active mutual fund ETF conversion on the Texas Stock Exchange. Brandon, thanks for joining me.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Inside Active》（洞察主动投资）——这是一档聚焦主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不满足于只言片语和标题式报道，而是更深入地探讨证券选择中的流程、挑战与理念。我是大卫·科恩（David Cohne），负责彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）的共同基金与主动投资研究。市场上一些最大的公司当初都是从很小的规模起步的，但投资中小盘成长型公司，并不仅仅是想找到下一家将会家喻户晓的企业。这些公司可能处于成长轨迹的更早期阶段，业绩记录尚不成熟，其业务最终会发展成什么样子也存在更大的不确定性。这既为主动管理者创造了机会，同时也让“判断哪些公司能够维持增长”以及——同样重要的——“市场对它们已有哪些预期”变得尤为关键。所以今天，我想探讨一位主动管理者如何应对这一挑战：如何在研究中识别潜在投资标的，如何将可持续增长与短期动能区分开来，预期和估值如何纳入选股考量，以及这些单独的投资想法最终如何汇聚成一个投资组合。今天与我一起探讨这个话题的，是布兰登·纳尔逊（Brandon Nelson），Calamos Investments（卡拉莫斯投资公司）的高级副总裁兼投资组合经理，管理着 Calamos Timpani 小盘成长共同基金（代码 CTSIX），以及 Calamos Timpani 主动型中小盘（SMID）成长策略——该策略本周刚刚从共同基金转换为 ETF，代码为 CTAG（C-T-A-G），实际上是德州证券交易所（Texas Stock Exchange）上首只由主动型共同基金转换而来的 ETF。布兰登，感谢你的到来。

turns.en: Yeah, thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 好的，谢谢你邀请我。

turns.en: So, you know, your investment philosophy is kind of described as fundamental momentum. What does that mean to you? And what does a company with fundamental momentum look like? Right.
turns.zh: 那么，你的投资理念常被概括为“基本面动能”（fundamental momentum）。这对你来说意味着什么？一家具备“基本面动能”的公司又是什么样子呢？

turns.en: It's really got two components to it. So the first component is sustainable growth. So companies that aren't just growing for a quarter or two, but have the sort of profile that they can sustain growth for many quarters and hopefully many years. That's part one of fundamental momentum. And part two is very importantly, companies that know how to manage expectations. So we're looking for underestimated growth as well. We want to invest in management teams that know what it's like to be in the public limelight. And it's very important to be able to Do what you say you're going to do. And we find that managing expectations is sometimes just as important as running the business and the operational side of things. So fast growth and underestimated growth equals fundamental momentum. Okay.
turns.zh: 它其实包含两个组成部分。第一个部分是可持续增长——也就是那些不只增长一两个季度，而是具备能够连续多个季度、乃至有望多年维持增长的特质的公司。这是“基本面动能”的第一部分。第二部分同样非常重要，那就是懂得如何管理预期的公司。所以我们也在寻找“被低估的增长”。我们希望投资于那些深知身处公众聚光灯下是什么滋味的管理团队。能够做到“说到做到”非常重要。我们发现，管理预期有时与经营业务、做好运营同等重要。所以，快速增长加上被低估的增长，就等于“基本面动能”。好的。

turns.en: And out of those two, what do you think is harder to identify and kind of what gives you the confidence that you're right when the market might be wrong?
turns.zh: 在这两者之中，你认为哪一个更难识别？另外，当市场可能判断错误时，是什么让你有信心相信自己是正确的？

turns.en: I think of the two underestimated growth is more difficult to find. Yeah. I think it's easier to identify, you know, open-ended fast growth situations, but it's a whole nother thing to execute on that and to, you know, again, do what you say you're going to do. And that I think is really, that's where our research comes into play. And we, we meet with a lot of management teams and we try to, sort of get inside their head and try to understand what's important to them so that we're looking for favorable setups where that sustainable growth profile is there, but also where management teams seem to have a sensitivity to managing expectations. And it's really when you get those two things together, that's where kind of the magic happens. The market really likes those characteristics, fast growth and underestimated growth. And it'll pay a premium for companies that have that profile. So we're all about trying to find companies that are in the early stages of demonstrating that profile and then riding that wave of them getting re-rated from maybe, let's say, a 14 times PE ratio when that process started. Fast forward seven, eight, nine quarters, and maybe you're trading at a PE ratio of 35 times. And that's where you really find the big winners.
turns.zh: 我认为在这两者之中，“被低估的增长”更难找到。是的。识别那些开放式的、快速增长的机会相对容易，但要真正去执行、去做到“说到做到”，那完全是另一回事。我认为这正是我们的研究发挥作用的地方。我们会见大量的管理团队，努力走进他们的内心，理解对他们来说什么才是重要的。这样我们就能寻找有利的投资布局——既有可持续增长的特质，同时管理团队似乎又对“管理预期”这件事抱有敏感度。只有当这两个因素结合在一起时，奇迹才会真正发生。市场非常喜欢这些特质——快速增长和被低估的增长——并愿意为具备这种特质的公司支付溢价。所以我们全力寻找的，是那些刚开始展现出这种特质、处于早期阶段的公司，然后乘着这股浪潮，伴随它们被重新估值——比如说，在这一过程启动时，它可能只有14倍的市盈率；七、八、九个季度之后，它的市盈率可能已经变成35倍。这才是你真正能发现大赢家的地方。

turns.en: Okay. You know, I've always heard a great company doesn't always turn out to be a great stock. How do you distinguish between the two when you're evaluating a potential company?
turns.zh: 好的。我一直听说，一家伟大的公司并不总能成为一只伟大的股票。在评估一家潜在投资标的时，你如何区分这两者？

turns.en: Yeah, I agree with that completely. Yeah, sometimes great companies are slow growing, not exceeding expectations. That doesn't mean you're a bad company if you're not showing fundamental momentum. But what we think drives stock prices the most, and at the end of the day, that's really what we care about as portfolio managers, is really what I said before. It's that fundamental momentum profile. And it's that fast growth and underestimated growth profile. And if you don't have it, you still might be a great company, but you're just not great for our portfolios. And you might be kind of a mediocre stock if you're not showing those characteristics.
turns.zh: 是的，我完全同意这个说法。有时候，伟大的公司增长缓慢，也不会超出预期。这并不意味着，如果你没有展现出“基本面动能”，你就不是一家好公司。但我们认为，最能驱动股价的因素——归根结底，作为投资组合经理，这才是我们真正关心的——正是我之前所说的那一点，也就是“基本面动能”的特质，即快速增长加上被低估的增长。如果你不具备这些，你或许仍然是一家伟大的公司，但对我们的投资组合而言，你并不出色。如果你没有展现出这些特征，你可能只会是一只表现平庸的股票。

turns.en: Okay. You know, you've been managing or investing in small and in SMID cap growth companies for a while. I don't want to age you, so I won't guess the year. But you've used essentially the similar philosophy throughout that period. What have you learned over that time about where the market is most likely to misprice growth?
turns.zh: 好的。你管理或投资小盘和中小盘（SMID）成长型公司已经有一段时间了。我不想暴露你的年龄，所以我就不猜具体年份了。但在这段时间里，你基本上一直沿用着相似的投资理念。在此期间，关于市场最容易在哪里对增长定价失误，你学到了什么？

turns.en: I think the most important maybe lesson I've learned in investing all those years, I don't know if it really answers your question directly about mispriced growth, but I think the, one of the first things I learned about investing, especially with this sort of investment process is sell discipline is really important and falling in love with your stocks is can be the kiss of death. And it's so easy to do. Just as humans, we have this tendency to get emotionally attached to stocks and we sort of lose our objectivity and we make bad decisions as a result. And we try to be unemotional and very objective. And we have this set of rules that relate to fundamental momentum. And when the companies violate those rules, you have to have an open mind and a willingness to reduce exposure to those stocks. Again, they might still be great companies, but they're possibly no longer going to be great stocks going forward. And it's important to distinguish between those two things. So biggest lesson learned is don't fall in love with your companies and have an open mind and a willingness to recognize the thesis may have changed from when you first purchased the stock and had success with the stock. And you have to just acknowledge that and know that, you know, going forward, it may not be wise to keep that investment in the portfolio.
turns.zh: 我认为，在这么多年的投资生涯中，我学到的最重要的一课——不知道这是否直接回答了你关于“被错误定价的增长”的问题——但我想，我最早学到的一点，尤其是针对这种投资流程而言，就是：卖出纪律真的非常重要，而“爱上自己的股票”可能是致命之吻。这件事太容易发生了。作为人，我们天生就有对股票产生情感依恋的倾向，从而失去客观性，进而做出糟糕的决定。我们努力做到不带情绪、保持高度客观。我们有一套与“基本面动能”相关的规则，当一家公司违反了这些规则时，你必须保持开放的心态，并且愿意削减对这些股票的仓位。同样，它们可能仍然是伟大的公司，但未来可能不再是伟大的股票了。区分这两者非常重要。所以，我学到的最大教训就是：不要爱上你投资的公司，要保持开放的心态，并愿意承认——投资逻辑可能已经与你最初买入这只股票、并在这只股票上获得成功时发生了变化。你必须承认这一点，并明白，展望未来，继续把这笔投资留在组合里可能并不明智。

turns.en: Okay. No, it makes a lot of sense. And, you know, we've kind of gone over the philosophy a little bit and set the stage. But, you know, one of the things I'd love to do on this podcast is kind of get into the whole process. So if you could kind of take us through your investment process from the beginning, you know, with thousands of small companies you could potentially invest in, you know, how do you narrow that new universe down to companies that deserve deeper research? Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 好的，这非常有道理。我们已经大致聊了聊投资理念，做了铺垫。而这档播客我很想做的一件事，就是深入探讨整个流程。那么，你能否从头带我们走一遍你的投资流程？面对成千上万家你潜在可投资的小公司，你如何把这个庞大的股票池缩小到那些值得深入研究的公司？

turns.en: And I'm glad you mentioned that because I think there's a perception that there really aren't many stocks available to choose from. You know, private equity has really become a big asset class over the years and it's legit, not knocking it, but there seems to be this narrative that, you know, companies, they're just, there's so few stocks for folks like me to even choose from. How could you possibly come up with a portfolio of stocks that could appreciate and value. And I can tell you again, from a 30-year perspective, there's no issue from where I sit. We're finding great ideas all over the place. Maybe there's fewer stocks public today than there were 10, 20 years ago, but there are still hundreds and hundreds of publicly traded stocks. And we're not dependent on IPOs, for instance, to come up with new ideas for our portfolio. So that's just kind of a side note, I guess, on what I'll tell you about our specific process. But yeah, you know, we start with a large opportunity set, call it 1500 plus stocks in the small cap and mid cap growth space. We have, you know, this tier one criteria. I mentioned this fundamental momentum criteria. We're really picky about the stocks we're choosing, you know, really only maybe about 10% of that universe of stocks. checks the boxes for what potentially could go in the portfolio. And it's from that sort of subset of, call it 150 to 200 stocks, where we really sort of roll up our sleeves and do much more in-depth research, myself and my teammates, to come up with a portfolio of 80 to 120 stocks. And so it's the fundamental momentum characteristics I mentioned, fast growth, underestimated growth, We also want to make sure the market is embracing the idea too. So we do pay attention to sort of the stocks, how the stock is being received in the marketplace. And we want to make sure the market is in a place where it's embracing that fundamental momentum that we're identifying. And it's really where you get the fundamental momentum marrying up with a market that's willing to embrace the idea. That's when you find the big winners. And so we're very much honed in on trying to find all those stars to sort of align. And we're good at finding big winners. And very importantly, we're good at letting them run. That's a big mistake investors make is they sell their winners too soon. And on the flip side, they keep their losers too long. Bad investment, you're hanging on to it, just hoping to get back to even someday. We look at it the other way. We say, wrong stock, wrong time. We run into trouble too, just like everybody else. But the way we handle it is sort of cut losses quickly, let it be a scratch or a bruise on the portfolio, but don't let it ruin the whole year. and double down and triple down on the exposure on a losing situation. So find big winners, let them run and cut your losers quickly. That's really the name of the game. And that's how we approach investing, you know, day to day. I'm covering a lot of ground with you just on, you know, investment process. Some of that is investment process and some of that is almost a investment philosophy, but it all kind of comes in together and intertwines on a day to day basis. So hopefully that helps explain. No, definitely.
turns.zh: 我很高兴你提到这一点，因为我认为有一种看法觉得，其实并没有多少股票可供选择。私募股权这些年的确已经成为一个庞大的资产类别，而且它是合理的，我不是在贬低它，但似乎存在这样一种论调：上市公司就那么点，像我这样的人根本没什么可选的，你又怎么可能组出一个能够增值的股票组合呢？我可以再次告诉你，站在30年的角度来看，从我所处的位置看，这根本不是问题。我们到处都能找到很好的投资点子。也许今天公开上市的公司比10年、20年前要少，但仍然有成百上千家公开交易的股票。而且，比如说，我们并不依赖 IPO 来为投资组合发掘新点子。所以，在向你介绍我们的具体流程之前，这只能算是我的一点题外话。不过，是的，我们是从一个庞大的机会集开始的——在小盘和中盘成长领域，姑且说是1500多只股票。我们有一套第一层（tier one）筛选标准，也就是我提到的“基本面动能”标准。我们对所选的股票非常挑剔，实际上，这个股票池里可能只有大约10%能够满足潜在纳入组合的条件。正是从这大约150到200只股票的子集中，我和我的团队才会真正卷起袖子，做远更深入的研究，从而构建出一个包含80到120只股票的投资组合。所以，靠的就是我提到的“基本面动能”特征——快速增长、被低估的增长；同时我们还希望确保市场也在接受这个投资逻辑。因此，我们确实会关注这些股票在市场上的接受度，希望确保市场处于一个愿意接纳我们所识别的“基本面动能”的状态。只有当“基本面动能”与一个愿意接纳这一逻辑的市场相结合时，你才能找到大赢家。所以我们非常专注于寻找所有这些“星星”能够连成一线的机会。我们善于发现大赢家，而且非常重要的是，我们善于让它们继续跑。投资者常犯的一个大错误就是过早卖出赢家，反过来，又把输家持有太久——一笔糟糕的投资，你死死抱着它，只是盼着有一天能回本。我们的看法正相反。我们会说：错误的股票，错误的时机。我们也会像所有人一样遇到麻烦，但我们的处理方式大致是快速止损，让它成为组合上的一道划痕或一处淤青，但不要让它毁掉一整年，也不要在一个亏损的头寸上加倍、再加倍地下注。所以，发现大赢家、让它们跑、快速砍掉输家——这才是真正的制胜之道，也是我们日复一日进行投资的方式。就投资流程这一点，我跟你讲了很多内容。其中一些属于投资流程，另一些几乎算是投资理念，但它们在日常操作中相互交织、融为一体。希望这能有助于解释清楚。——不，绝对解释清楚了。

turns.en: It, You alluded to management earlier, and I'm going to ask you about that next. But, you know, is there once these companies have your attention, you know, what exactly are you looking at to kind of give you those answers that you might not get just from looking at financial statements?
turns.zh: 你刚才提到了管理层，接下来我正想问这个。不过，一旦这些公司进入了你的关注范围，具体来说，你会考察哪些东西，来获得那些仅凭查看财务报表可能得不到的答案？

turns.en: Yeah, as it relates to management teams, especially in the small cap space, you know, management teams are a really big deal. They tend to move the needle a lot in terms of how the stock is actually going to ultimately perform. And it really relates, I'd say the most to that idea of underestimated growth, you know, management teams, there's some management teams and I've seen it all over the years where on one extreme, they'll say, you know, we have, we don't really care what the market looks at. We don't, we don't care if our growth is underestimated or not. We're just going to do what we're going to do. And if it's better than people think, so be it. If it's worse than people expect, so be it. We don't care. Like that's, red flags all over the place for us if we're hearing that. If instead they're like, okay, we've got a conservative philosophical approach, we've given guidance, but we've not included a new product that we're rolling out next year because we don't know how good that product is going to be and therefore just out of conservatism, let's just not include it. And so they're very cognizant of sort of this idea of managing expectations and making sure they don't fall short of whatever the expectations are that are out there. So that's where the management team, I think, probably shows itself the most in the importance of management teams. And that ripples through to the sell side analyst estimates too. Let's face it, a lot of these analysts that are publishing research are using management's sort of guidance to determine where their models should end up being. And so there's this sort of domino effect of, You know, management teams that are conservative and have sensitivity to managing expectations, they tend to be, you know, just very important on a lot of levels, I guess, in terms of, you know, checking the box of fundamental momentum.
turns.zh: 是的，就管理团队而言，尤其是在小盘领域，管理团队真的是至关重要。就一只股票最终实际表现如何来说，他们往往能产生很大的影响。我想说，这一点与“被低估的增长”这个理念关系最为密切。关于管理团队——这些年来我见过各种各样的情况：一个极端是，有些管理团队会说：“我们其实并不在意市场怎么看，我们不在乎自己的增长是否被低估。我们该怎么做就怎么做。如果结果比人们想的更好，那也无所谓；如果比人们预期的更差，那也无所谓，我们不在乎。”如果我们听到这种话，那对我们来说就是遍地亮红灯。反之，如果他们是这样的：“好的，我们秉持一种保守的理念，我们给出了业绩指引，但并没有把明年即将推出的一款新产品纳入其中，因为我们不知道这款产品会有多好，所以出于保守起见，干脆就不把它算进去。”这样一来，他们对“管理预期”这个理念就有非常清醒的认识，确保自己不会低于市场上已有的任何预期。我认为，管理团队的重要性正是在这一点上体现得最为充分。而这种影响还会波及到卖方分析师的预测。坦白说，很多发布研究报告的分析师，都是依据管理层给出的指引来决定自己的模型最终应该落在什么水平。所以就形成了这样一种多米诺骨牌效应：那些保守、且对管理预期抱有敏感度的管理团队，在很多层面上都非常重要——就“基本面动能”这一勾选项而言，我想尤其如此。

turns.en: With the, you know, underestimated growth, how do you measure what the market already expects from a company? And, you know, how large, I guess, is the gap between your expectations and the market needs or what the market expects, you know, for it to actually become interesting?
turns.zh: 说到“被低估的增长”，你如何衡量市场对一家公司已有的预期？另外，你的预期与市场预期之间的差距，大概要达到多大，才会真正变得有吸引力？

turns.en: No, that's a good point because if it's just a minor upside situation, let's say the company is expected to grow 10% and we think they're really going to do 11%, I don't know if that's enough to get us excited. But if it's 10% growth expected, but we think they're going to do 23%, okay, now that's much more meaningful. And I'm talking like over the course of a year. that's likely to result in that valuation multiple expansion that I mentioned earlier, where if the company's growing fast and exceeding expectations meaningfully, that's going to have a direct result in terms of the magnitude of that re-rating that the stock is likely to see. So it is important. We look for fast growth, but we also look for underestimated growth. And just to really bring the point home, You know, we would actually pass on a faster growth situation where there's minimal upside. So I would not buy a stock that's growing where the company's growing 40%, but they're likely to do, you know, actually put up 37% growth. I would pass on that stock. I'd rather buy a stock where growth is expected to be 18% and they're going to do 25% growth, lower growth rates in that example. but underestimated growth. And so that's really, again, where kind of the magic happens. So you have to have a growth rate above a minimum for in sort of a normalized economy. We like to see at least 10% revenue growth, at least 15% earnings per share growth. Averages are much higher than that, but that's kind of what we're thinking for a minimum growth rate. And then for revision potential, I'd say at least 10% revision, positive revision potential over the course of the four or 12 months.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题，因为如果只是小幅的上行空间——比如说，市场预期一家公司增长10%，而我们认为它实际能做到11%——我不确定这是否足以让我们兴奋。但如果市场预期增长10%，而我们认为它能做到23%，好，那就有意义得多了。我这里说的是一年左右的时间跨度。这很可能带来我之前提到的估值倍数扩张：如果一家公司快速增长并大幅超出预期，那就会直接决定这只股票可能经历的重新估值的幅度。所以这一点很重要。我们寻找快速增长，但同时也寻找被低估的增长。为了把这一点讲透——实际上，我们会放弃那种虽然增长更快、但上行空间很小的机会。所以，我不会买这样一只股票：一家公司增长40%，但它实际可能只交出37%的增长。我会放弃这只股票。我宁愿买这样一只股票：预期增长18%，而它实际能做到25%——在这个例子里增长率更低，但增长被低估了。所以，这又回到了那个“奇迹发生”的地方。因此，在一个大致正常的经济环境下，你的增长率必须高于某个最低门槛。我们希望看到至少10%的营收增长、至少15%的每股收益增长。平均值远高于此，但这大致就是我们对最低增长率的考量。至于盈利预测的上调潜力，我会说，在四个月或12个月的时间里，至少有10%的正向上调潜力。

turns.en: That's interesting. How does valuation fit into the equation? I mean, can you have a company that has exactly what you're looking for, but might just be simply too expensive to own?
turns.zh: 很有意思。那么估值是如何纳入这个考量的呢？我是说，会不会有这样一家公司，它完全符合你要找的特质，但单纯就是太贵了，不值得持有？

turns.en: We do pay attention to valuation, but it is not a tier one sort of consideration. We don't let valuation sort of drive the bus on our decision making. A lot of stocks that look expensive are stud performers, right? They end up being monster performers despite looking expensive. And part of the issue is, yeah, they might look expensive on the consensus estimates, but they reported way more than the consensus estimates. And so what looked to be a high valuation multiple at the time you were looking at it ended up not really being that high when you plugged in what they really ended up doing in earnings. These are stocks that get valued on forward earnings and forward EBITDA. expectations, forward sales. And so to the extent there's upside to all those metrics, there's downside to the valuation. So evaluation can be kind of tricky. Again, we pay attention to it. We get most nervous about stocks where we're sensing fatigue in the fundamental momentum profile at the same time that we're seeing elevated valuation multiples. So maybe it's already gone through that re-rating process, that positive re-rating process. And now we're starting to see some fatigue and maybe a little weakness in that fundamental momentum profile. It's time to reduce exposure when we see those characteristics all kind of come into play. So again, we use it, but we don't let it trick us. Valuation, that is, we don't let it trick us into not buying stocks that look expensive up front. At the same time, sometimes valuation tricks people into not selling their losers. They say, oh, I can't sell this stock It's so cheap. Well, maybe it's not as cheap as it looks because that company is going to miss estimates in the multiples a lot higher than it looks. So it can go the other way, too. So I think valuation just I just don't think it should be a sort of decision. I don't think it should drive by and to sell. And I don't think it should drive by or sell decisions. There we go.
turns.zh: 我们确实会关注估值，但它不是第一层（tier one）的考量因素。我们不会让估值来主导我们的决策。很多看起来昂贵的股票其实是优等生，对吧？尽管看着贵，它们最终却成了表现极其出色的“怪兽级”股票。部分原因在于：是的，以市场一致预期来看它们可能显得昂贵，但它们实际的业绩远超一致预期。所以，在你观察时看起来很高的估值倍数，当你把它们实际赚到的盈利代入后，最终其实并没有那么高。这些股票是基于前瞻盈利、前瞻 EBITDA（息税折旧摊销前利润）预期和前瞻营收来估值的。因此，只要这些指标存在上行空间，估值倍数就会有下行空间。所以估值可能相当微妙。同样，我们会关注它。最让我们紧张的，是那些我们感觉到“基本面动能”特质正在显现疲态、同时估值倍数又处于高位的股票。也就是说，它可能已经完成了那个正向的重新估值过程，如今我们开始看到“基本面动能”出现一些疲态、甚至有点走弱。当这些特征同时显现时，就该削减仓位了。所以，我们会用估值，但不会让它骗到我们——也就是说，我们不会因为它而不敢去买那些一开始看起来昂贵的股票。与此同时，估值有时也会骗人，让人不肯卖出亏损的股票。他们会说：“哦，我不能卖这只股票，它太便宜了。”但也许它并不像看起来那么便宜，因为那家公司将会不及预期，其估值倍数远没有看上去那么低。所以情况也可能反过来。因此，我认为估值——我只是觉得它不应该成为决策的驱动因素，不应该主导买入和卖出的决定。就是这样。

turns.en: Okay, no, makes sense. You know, I mean, smaller companies, I think, can, you know, they obviously have tremendous growth opportunities, but, you know, some of them also can have, you know, greater business or financing risk. How do you kind of distinguish between a company that's, you know, early in, you know, say a durable growth trajectory versus one that, you know, where the numbers simply look good temporarily?
turns.zh: 好的，这很有道理。我的意思是，小公司显然拥有巨大的增长机会，但其中一些也可能面临更大的经营或融资风险。你如何区分这样两种公司：一种是刚刚踏上（比如说）一条可持续增长轨迹的公司，另一种则是数字只是暂时好看的公司？

turns.en: Yeah, as far as like financing goes, you know, most of the stocks we invest in, a lot of them are self-funding their growth. And that's important. And for the ones that aren't able to self-fund their growth, maybe their earlier stage, they're still building out their infrastructure, let's say, they've got something special, at least the ones we invested. And investors are very willing to get capital to them in order for them to build their business. These aren't just like plain vanilla, you know, small companies and mid-sized companies. These are up and coming companies. companies that have something special, some unique good or service that they're selling. And investors are excited to give them capital to build their business. And so I find that it's not usually an issue. Well, first of all, our companies that we invest in do tend to be much more profitable than the average small cap company. So that's something I probably should have said right off the bat. And they also tend to have less financial leverage. But in cases where they need capital, They usually don't have a problem getting it because they're very exciting, sort of sexy growth stocks where investors are seeing a really positive potential return on that capital. Okay.
turns.zh: 是的，就融资而言，我们投资的大多数股票中，很多都是靠自身资金来支撑增长的，这一点很重要。而对于那些无法自筹资金支持增长的公司，也许它们处于更早的阶段，比如说仍在搭建自己的基础设施——但至少我们投资的那些，它们都拥有某种特别的东西。投资者非常乐意为它们提供资金，以帮助它们发展业务。这些并不是那种平淡无奇的小公司或中型公司，而是冉冉升起的新星，是拥有某种特别之处、销售某种独特产品或服务的公司。投资者很乐意为它们提供资金来发展业务。所以我发现，这通常不是个问题。而且，首先，我们投资的公司往往比一般的小盘公司盈利能力强得多——这一点我或许一开始就该说明。它们的财务杠杆通常也更低。但在需要资金的情况下，它们通常也不难拿到资金，因为它们是非常令人兴奋、颇具吸引力的成长股，投资者看到这些资金有望带来非常可观的潜在回报。好的。

turns.en: Once you have a company that meets all of your criteria, how do you determine the position size in a portfolio? What would earn a stock a large position?
turns.zh: 一旦你找到一家符合你所有标准的公司，你如何确定它在组合中的仓位大小？什么样的因素能让一只股票获得较大仓位？

turns.en: Great question. It does depend on, you know, maybe the history we have with the stock. If we've owned it before and we're more familiar with it, there's a willingness to maybe make it a bigger position faster. But I'd say for most situations, you know, we'll start at maybe a 50 basis point position in the portfolio and then we'll watch it closely. We'll, you know, we have our finger on the pulse of these companies and, you know, we're paying attention to all the data points. We're scrubbing the quarterly earnings reports, and we're just going from there. At the same time, we're also monitoring the market reception to those stocks too. And we're monitoring those data points on a daily basis. And so if maybe it starts at 50 basis points and we see a great quarter of execution, let's say it's growing fast, beating expectations, there's very much a willingness to take it up to maybe a 1% or 1.3% position in the portfolio and then go from there. Hopefully it's appreciating at the same time. And so you end up seeing this sort of natural lift of weight in the portfolio as a company, as the quarters go by and the execution is there and the company is being embraced by the market, that 50 basis point position evolves between the market appreciation and us buying more. Before you know it, sometimes it's, you know, 2% plus position, you know, within six months. And so that's very common for it to sort of play out that way. And then, of course, you know, very, again, cannot emphasize enough the importance of sell discipline and just, you know, monitoring the portfolio constantly. One thing I didn't mention before, which is really important, everybody probably always says, you know, they're great at buying stocks and great at selling stocks. We actually took it another level when we're talking about our sell discipline. The thesis was, or the theory was, hey, if we're so great at selling stocks, they probably should be poor performers after we sell them. Well, the data supports that. We ran all that. We've been running that data for years. And sure enough, stocks we sell out of our portfolio persist as losers in the six months after we sell it, 12 months after we sell it, and not just by a little bit. They end up being you know, meaningful losers relative to our benchmark. So there's just to add some meat to the bones, I guess, to say the sell discipline adds a lot of value. I think we're really good at buying stocks and letting them run, but I think we're exceptionally good at selling stocks and, you know, avoiding trouble or lessening trouble.
turns.zh: 问得好。这确实取决于——比如说我们与这只股票的历史渊源。如果我们以前持有过它、对它更熟悉，就会更愿意更快地把它建成一个较大的仓位。但我要说，在大多数情况下，我们也许会先从组合中50个基点（0.5%）的仓位起步，然后密切观察它。我们会时刻紧盯这些公司的脉搏，关注所有的数据点，仔细研读季度财报，然后据此推进。与此同时，我们也会监测市场对这些股票的接受度，并且每天都在跟踪这些数据点。所以，如果它从50个基点起步，而我们看到一个执行得非常出色的季度——比如说它快速增长、超出预期——我们就非常愿意把它提升到组合中大约1%或1.3%的仓位，然后再往上走。但愿它同时在升值。于是你会看到，随着一个个季度过去、执行到位、公司受到市场青睐，这只股票在组合中的权重会自然抬升——那50个基点的仓位，会在市场升值和我们加仓的共同作用下不断演变。不知不觉间，有时在六个月之内，它就成了2%以上的仓位。这种情况这样演变是非常常见的。然后，当然，我再次怎么强调卖出纪律的重要性、以及持续监控组合的重要性都不为过。有一件我之前没提、但其实非常重要的事：每个人可能都总会说自己既擅长买股票、又擅长卖股票。而在谈到卖出纪律时，我们实际上把它提升到了另一个层次。这个论点——或者说这个理论——是：嘿，如果我们真的这么擅长卖股票，那么被我们卖出之后，这些股票很可能应该表现不佳。而数据支持这一点。我们把这些都跑了一遍，多年来一直在跟踪这些数据。果然，我们从组合中卖出的股票，在卖出后的六个月、十二个月里持续表现为输家，而且不只是差一点点，相对于我们的基准，它们最终成了名副其实的输家。所以，这算是给“卖出纪律创造了很多价值”这个说法增添了一些实打实的佐证。我认为我们确实很擅长买股票并让它们跑，但我认为我们尤其擅长卖股票，从而避开麻烦或减轻麻烦。

turns.en: I'm not hearing, you're not planning on adding a short component, are you? Like a shorting component?
turns.zh: 我听下来，你并不打算加入做空的部分，对吧？比如一个做空的组件？

turns.en: No, we've been asked that. We have been asked that many times over the years.
turns.zh: 不，这个问题别人问过我们。这些年来，我们被问过很多次。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: We maybe should have done that a long time ago, but no, we're long only. But yeah, it's a logical follow-up question. We probably should be shorting those stocks that we're selling because again, if they're falling later.
turns.zh: 也许我们早就该那么做了，但不，我们只做多。不过，是的，这是个合乎逻辑的追问。我们或许应该做空那些我们卖出的股票，因为同样地，如果它们之后会下跌的话。

turns.en: That's pretty cool. I mean, that's obviously a different type of skill, but it's cool that it works that way. When I was going through the documentation of the two strategies, one of the things that kind of struck out or struck out for me or that I noticed was kind of in the SPID strategy, it said you expect roughly 90% of the value added to come from security selection rather than sector kind of allocations. So I guess my question is, how do you keep a bottom-up portfolio like this from unintentionally becoming a large bet on a particular sector or even a factor?
turns.zh: 这挺酷的。我的意思是，这显然是一种不同类型的技能，但它能以这种方式奏效，还是很酷的。当我翻看这两个策略的说明文件时，有一件事让我印象深刻，或者说我注意到——在中小盘（SMID）策略里，它写道：你预计大约90%的附加值来自证券选择，而非行业配置之类。所以我想我的问题是：你如何防止这样一个自下而上的组合，无意中变成对某个特定行业、甚至某个因子的大额押注？

turns.en: It's always a mixture of sector, or sorry, selection and sector allocation. exposures and factor exposures, of course, where we spend our time is on and where we think we add the most value is on the bottom up, you know, company interactions and just having our finger on the pulse. We're intentionally trying to find stocks that aren't that sensitive to the Fed's next move or GDP being, you know, plus one or plus three percent. You know, it's just it's we want to find stocks that are really in their own bull market and you know, have that profile where they're going to grow fast. They're going to likely beat and raise. And the macro is just kind of a rounding error on what, what that outcome is going to be. It's, it's not that they're immune from the macro, but maybe the macro, a bad macro knocks the 25% growth down to 23%. But it doesn't derail the growth profile meaningfully. So that's where we spend our time. I think that's where we add the most value. The sector exposures are really just a fallout of that bottom-up effort. And we're not afraid to have deviation from our benchmarks as far as sector exposure. So that inevitably does result in some value add or value subtraction at the sector level. But it's really the portfolio decisions are driven mostly by bottom-up research and really the outlook for these company-specific situations. But, you know, we do have themes. You know, AI infrastructure has been a pretty big theme for us the last three years. That shows up in some of the technology exposure and industrial exposure. So that's definitely elevated the sector weights in those two sectors over the last three years or so. But it's, you know, it also, it doesn't have to be thematic either. You know, our financial services exposure right now is, higher than it normally would be and it's just because we happen to have found a few kind of one-off financial services stocks that meet the fundamental momentum growth profile and that's taken the sector weight up and so you know to some extent financials as at the sector level is going to be showing up as a value adder detractor within our sector sector attribution but It's not the primary focus. It's really, again, more of the company specific bottom up focus that drives the value add.
turns.zh: 它永远是选股、行业配置敞口以及因子敞口的混合体。当然，我们花时间最多、也认为最能创造价值的地方，是自下而上的公司层面互动，以及时刻紧盯脉搏。我们是刻意去寻找那些对美联储下一步动作、或对 GDP 是增长1%还是3%并不那么敏感的股票。我们想找到的是那种真正处于自己牛市之中的股票，具备那种将快速增长、很可能“超预期并上调指引”的特质，而宏观因素对最终结果而言不过是个可以忽略不计的零头。这并不是说它们对宏观免疫，而是说，也许糟糕的宏观环境会把25%的增长拉低到23%，但它不会实质性地让增长轨迹脱轨。所以这就是我们投入精力的地方，我认为这也是我们创造最多价值的地方。行业敞口其实只是这种自下而上努力的自然结果。在行业敞口方面，我们并不害怕偏离基准。所以这不可避免地会在行业层面带来一些附加价值或价值减损。但真正驱动组合决策的，主要是自下而上的研究，以及对这些公司个体情形的前景判断。不过，我们确实也有一些主题。比如说，AI 基础设施在过去三年里一直是我们一个相当重要的主题，它体现在我们的部分科技敞口和工业敞口上。所以这确实抬高了这两个行业在过去大约三年里的行业权重。但它也不必然是主题性的。比如说，我们目前的金融服务敞口高于平常水平，这只是因为我们碰巧发现了几只比较个例的、符合“基本面动能”增长特质的金融服务类股票，从而推高了该行业的权重。所以在一定程度上，金融板块在行业层面会在我们的行业归因中体现为一个附加值或减损项，但这并不是我们的主要关注点。真正驱动附加价值的，还是那种针对具体公司的、自下而上的关注。

turns.en: So, you know, I did want to also ask kind of the difference between the portfolios, obviously you have a small cap and then the SMID. And, you know, how does expanding the opportunity set from small caps into mid caps kind of change the types of companies you find and the way you construct that portfolio?
turns.zh: 那么，我确实也想问一下这两个组合之间的区别——显然你有一只小盘基金，还有一只中小盘（SMID）基金。把机会集从小盘扩展到中盘，会如何改变你所找到的公司类型，以及你构建组合的方式？

turns.en: Yeah. And we've had mid cap, you know, we've invested in mid caps for most of my career. Um, I think mid caps inherently, because they're a little bit more mature than the small cap companies, they, they sometimes aren't growing as fast. You know, they tend to have more analyst coverage. Um, and so there's probably less inefficiency, uh, in terms of, you know, where those stocks are priced, but there, I, you know, my career, we have found some huge mid cap winners as well. So, um, I think what we do works really well in small growth and mid-growth. And that's, yeah, it's just more of a matter of sort of how extreme is the sort of inefficiency at the mid-cap level versus small cap level. And it's still extreme enough where I think there's opportunities to exploit. So I think it makes a lot of sense to have exposure to both. And we've had a lot of success. investing in Bullock over the years.
turns.zh: 是的。我们一直有中盘基金——在我职业生涯的大部分时间里，我们都投资中盘股。我认为，中盘股本质上，因为它们比小盘公司更成熟一些，有时增长得没那么快。它们往往有更多的分析师覆盖，所以从这些股票的定价来看，无效定价的程度可能更低。但在我职业生涯中，我们也发现过一些巨大的中盘赢家。所以，我认为我们的做法在小盘成长和中盘成长领域都非常奏效。是的，这更多地取决于中盘层面的无效定价相对于小盘层面有多极端。而这种无效程度依然足够极端，我认为存在可利用的机会。所以我觉得同时持有两者的敞口非常有道理。这些年来，我们在投资这两类股票上都取得了很大的成功。

turns.en: Makes sense. You know, one of the things I've been observing and, you know, my colleagues have as well, and I've actually written about it a little bit is, you know, small caps really have spent much of the past decade lagging their large cap peers. And, you know, but the relative performance has kind of changed a bit, you know, over the last few months and this year. And, you know, from the perspective of a stock picker, do you think the, has the quality of the opportunity set in small cap growth changed? recently?
turns.zh: 有道理。我一直观察到的一点——我的同事们也是如此，而且我自己也写过一些——就是：在过去十年的大部分时间里，小盘股确实一直落后于大盘股同行。但最近几个月、以及今年，这种相对表现有所改变。那么，从一位选股者的角度来看，你认为近期小盘成长领域机会集的质量是否发生了变化？

turns.en: I don't think so. I guess that touches a little bit maybe on the earlier conversation of perception that there's a scarcity of ideas. You're right though. Small caps have lagged large caps for, it's actually been nine years in a row. If you can believe it, the Russell 2000 has lagged the Russell 1000. I don't know if that's so much that small caps have been bad as so much as the mega caps have been just sensational. But you're right. Things have changed. Really, you could almost pinpoint it to a day specifically last year in 2025. It was, you know, I think it was April 9th or something like that is when small caps started to take more of a leadership role. And this is just I'm speaking relative now. It's not that large caps have gone down. But, you know, looking back like 100 years or so, you'll see small caps will lead over large caps for decades. multiple years in a row and then large caps will lead over small caps for multiple years in a row and they take turns. So this could be, you know, early days of a big up cycle for small caps, you know, probably a little bit too soon to say, but very importantly, the earnings are there and everyone's probably, you know, we've heard a lot of talk in recent months about this is a very strong earnings environment. It's been strong for small caps as well as large caps and mid caps. But the difference, I guess, and maybe what's finally happening here is, you know, small caps have looked really inexpensive relative to large caps for many years, but they didn't have the earnings momentum. And that was kind of the missing piece. And that's why they stayed cheap for so long. They're still cheap. They're not quite as cheap as they were relative to large caps, but importantly, they have tremendous earnings momentum. They're scheduled to grow, and these numbers change all the time, but small caps are scheduled to grow about 15% in 2026 and are poised to accelerate to about 17% last I looked in 2027. So those are great growth rates, and to actually see an acceleration of growth expected at least in 2027, it might cause small caps to close the gap even further with large caps in terms of the valuation. And it could lead to a sustained... leadership in small caps but what I like about what we do is you know we're not dependent on that happening for us to win again we're all about bottom up stock picking and positioning and you know small caps lagged large caps big time in 2024 in 2025 and we put up big time points on the board. Despite that, you know, we didn't need small caps to beat large caps for us to do well. And this year we're doing very well and small caps are beating large caps. And so it's, it's, it doesn't determine necessarily what, how we're going to do, but I think it would, you know, it would probably be a tailwind overall if small caps sustained a leadership role going forward, but it's tough to predict that. And I'm glad we're not living and dying with, with that happening.
turns.zh: 我不这么认为。我想这在某种程度上又回到了我们之前谈到的那种“点子稀缺”的看法。不过你说得对。小盘股落后于大盘股——实际上已经连续九年了。信不信由你，罗素2000指数（Russell 2000）一直落后于罗素1000指数（Russell 1000）。我不知道这与其说是小盘股表现差，不如说是超大盘股的表现实在太惊艳了。但你说得对，情况确实变了。真的，你几乎可以精确到具体某一天——就在去年，2025年。我记得大概是4月9日前后，从那时起小盘股开始更多地扮演领涨角色。我这里说的是相对表现，并不是说大盘股下跌了。但如果你回溯大约100年，你会看到小盘股会连续多年、乃至数十年领先于大盘股，然后大盘股又会连续多年领先于小盘股，它们轮流坐庄。所以，这可能是小盘股一轮大上行周期的早期阶段——现在下这个判断可能还有点太早。但非常重要的是，盈利已经跟上了。近几个月来，大家可能都听到很多说法，说这是一个非常强劲的盈利环境。无论对小盘股、大盘股还是中盘股来说，盈利都很强劲。但区别——我想也是这里终于正在发生的变化——在于：多年来小盘股相对于大盘股看起来非常便宜，但它们缺乏盈利动能。这就是那块缺失的拼图，也是它们长时间保持低估的原因。它们现在依然便宜，虽然相对于大盘股没有以前那么便宜了，但重要的是，它们拥有巨大的盈利动能。它们的增长已被排上日程——这些数字随时都在变，但据我上次查看，小盘股预计在2026年增长约15%，并有望在2027年加速到约17%。这些都是很棒的增长率，而且如果真的看到增长加速——至少在2027年——这可能会促使小盘股在估值上进一步缩小与大盘股的差距，并可能带来小盘股持续的领涨地位。但我喜欢我们所做的事情的一点是：我们要想赢，并不依赖于这种情况的发生。我们靠的是自下而上的选股和布局。要知道，在2024年和2025年，小盘股大幅落后于大盘股，而尽管如此，我们还是拿到了相当亮眼的成绩。我们并不需要小盘股跑赢大盘股才能表现良好。而今年我们表现得非常好，同时小盘股也在跑赢大盘股。所以，这并不必然决定我们会表现如何，但我认为，如果小盘股未来能持续扮演领涨角色，整体上大概会是一股顺风。不过这很难预测。我很庆幸，我们并不把身家性命押在这件事是否会发生上。

turns.zh: 我认为他们只是低估了其潜力。小盘股作为一个资产类别，遍地都是未来的大赢家。是的，暗处也潜伏着大输家。所以这个机会是巨大的。但你必须小心，必须精挑细选，必须有非常严格的卖出纪律。所以，如果你要交易那种既有巨大上行、又有巨大下行潜力的股票，你最好有一套严格的卖出纪律来管理风险。这些我们都具备。但我觉得总体而言，人们似乎普遍对小盘股非常不屑。他们找出各种理由来干脆无视这个资产类别：“哦，利率在上升，那就意味着小盘股要归零了，对吧？”“不，现在没有 IPO 了，那一定意味着你没有任何投资点子，对吧？因为你完全依赖 IPO 市场。”这完全是错的。我们几乎根本不依赖 IPO 市场来产生新点子，它在新点子生成潜力中不过是个可以忽略不计的零头。所以我觉得，市面上可能存在一些懒惰的思维——他们几乎是想否定小盘股这个资产类别。但我认为这是个巨大的错误，因为还是那句话，大赢家就出在那里，在小盘领域找到大赢家的可能性，要比在大盘领域高得多。所以这是一个非常值得关注的资产类别。而且我也是言行一致、真金白银投入的。我个人有相当多的资金投在我们管理的这些中小盘股票基金里——也许，嗯，投得有点多，但这就是——我的看法是：不管利率怎么走都无所谓。在我看来，关键就是：这些是定价无效的股票，到处都是“本垒打”般的潜力。但要说清楚，这确实是一个需要技巧、难以驾驭的资产类别，你得知道自己在做什么。而且，我坚信我们正在做的事情。这是一套经过验证、可复制的流程，我们已经执行了30多年。我认为结果已经证明了这一点。
